years_since_diagnosis.evidence: diagnosed with Crohn's five years ago

disease_control.evidence: Life is manageable. Not great, but manageable — on Humira two years, but still has fatigue, joint pain, frequent infections, and is being prepared for possible switch to Stelara

treatments.reason_stopped: Sent blood sugars through roof; tapered after two months
treatments.evidence: Started triple therapy - prednisone, azathioprine, and mesalamine. Prednisone sent blood sugars through roof. Tapered prednisone after two months.

treatments.reason_stopped: Crohn's flared when methotrexate was started; implied azathioprine was replaced
treatments.evidence: Azathioprine and mesalamine maintained remission for about a year. Then started having severe joint pain... GI doctor switched approach.
Started methotrexate for both conditions. Helped joints but Crohn's flared.
Finally approved for Humira... Been on Humira two years. Life is manageable.

encounters.evidence: Primary care ran basic tests, all normal except elevated CRP. Referred to gastroenterologist.
Referred to gastroenterologist... Colonoscopy revealed severe ileocolonic Crohn's... Finally agreed to biologics... Finally approved for Humira.
Rheumatologist said it's enteropathic arthritis, related to Crohn's.
Endocrinologist had to add insulin to my diabetes regimen.

status.evidence: Finally approved for Humira. Been on Humira two years.

barriers.evidence: Insurance nightmare began. Required documentation of failure of multiple therapies. Appeals process took four months.
The co-pay even with insurance - $400 monthly. Thank god for manufacturer assistance program.

referral_steps_gp_to_prescriber.evidence: GP referred to GI specialist who ultimately prescribed Humira — 2 steps (GP -> GI)

extraction_notes: Insulin added for diabetes management (not Crohn's treatment) — excluded from treatments. Nutritionist visit noted but not included as a Crohn's treatment encounter. Stelara mentioned as a future contingency if Humira fails, but patient is currently on Humira and no switch has been initiated; biologic.status remains 'on'. Azathioprine and mesalamine were used concurrently initially; sequence reflects approximate order of introduction and discontinuation.
